title: Paddling equipment: overview
description: Paddling equipment essentials: boat, paddle. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. The right gear does three things: keeps you safe, lets you perform, and lasts. Beginners should spend on safety and fit first — the best equipment is the kind you forget you are wearing because it fits perfectly and does its job.

title: Gear 1: boat
description: In Paddling, the boat matters more than beginners think. Fit is everything — wrong size ruins performance and risks injury. Quality gear lasts years when cared for; neglected gear fails at the worst moment.

title: Footwear
d: Paddling footwear must suit the surface.
definition: Paddling footwear must suit the surface.
description: Footwear for Paddling: matched to the surface, fitted to the foot, replaced on schedule. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. The wrong shoes cause the most common overuse injuries in sport. Break new pairs in gradually, keep them dry between sessions, and retire them when the support dies — usually long before they look worn.

title: Protective gear
d: Protection in Paddling is mandatory where the laws require it.
definition: Protection in Paddling is mandatory where the laws require it.
description: Protective gear in Paddling: helmets, guards, and padding exist because the injury patterns are known. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Wear every required piece, every session — the one rep you skip is the one that finds you. Replace protective gear after any serious impact; its job was to die so you did not.

title: Apparel
d: Paddling kit: built for movement, weather, and team identity.
definition: Paddling kit: built for movement, weather, and team identity.
description: Apparel for Paddling: moisture-wicking, unrestricted, and weather-appropriate. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Team kits carry identity — wear them with pride and keep them clean. In heat, light colors and ventilation; in cold, layers you can shed. Never let clothing restrict the movements the sport demands.

title: Training aids
d: Train Paddling smarter with cones, targets, and video.
definition: Train Paddling smarter with cones, targets, and video.
description: Training aids for Paddling: cones, targets, rebounders, and video turn good sessions into great ones. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. The best aid is often the simplest — a wall, a target, a stopwatch. Buy aids that fix your specific weakness, not the gadget of the month.

title: Maintenance
d: Maintain Paddling gear: clean, dry, inspect, store.
definition: Maintain Paddling gear: clean, dry, inspect, store.
description: Maintenance for Paddling equipment: clean after use, dry fully before storage, inspect before every session, store out of sun and damp. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. A five-minute routine doubles gear life. Keep a small repair kit — tape, laces, patches — because failures happen at venues, not at home.

title: Fitting guide
d: Fit Paddling gear properly: the performance multiplier.
definition: Fit Paddling gear properly: the performance multiplier.
description: Fitting Paddling gear: the difference between good and great equipment is usually fit. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Get fitted by someone who knows the sport, re-check fit as young athletes grow, and never borrow safety gear. If it moves, pinches, or distracts, it does not fit.

title: Safety standards
d: Paddling gear must meet certification standards.
definition: Paddling gear must meet certification standards.
description: Safety standards for Paddling: look for the certification marks — they mean the gear passed real tests. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Counterfeit safety gear kills; buy from reputable sources. Standards update over time; replace gear that predates current certifications.

title: Youth gear
d: Young Paddling athletes need sized-down, not dumbed-down, gear.
definition: Young Paddling athletes need sized-down, not dumbed-down, gear.
description: Youth Paddling gear: sized for growing bodies, never adult hand-me-downs that do not fit. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Kids outgrow gear fast — buy adjustable where possible and check fit monthly. Never compromise on helmets or protection to save money; skimp on the bag, not the brain bucket.

title: Budget guide
d: Equip for Paddling at any budget: spend on safety first.
definition: Equip for Paddling at any budget: spend on safety first.
description: Budgeting Paddling gear: spend first on protection and fit, then on the implement, last on accessories. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Good used gear beats bad new gear for non-safety items. Plan the yearly replacement cycle so costs never surprise you mid-season.

title: Innovations
d: Paddling equipment keeps evolving: materials, data, and design.
definition: Paddling equipment keeps evolving: materials, data, and design.
description: Innovation in Paddling gear: lighter materials, smarter design, and embedded data. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Adopt innovations that solve your problem; ignore the rest until proven. The fundamentals — fit, safety, durability — outlast every trend.

title: Rules on equipment
d: The laws of Paddling regulate equipment specifications.
definition: The laws of Paddling regulate equipment specifications.
description: Equipment rules in Paddling: the laws specify what is legal — dimensions, materials, and sometimes brands. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Check legality before competition; illegal gear means disqualification. When in doubt, ask an official before the event, not during it.

title: Equipment checklist
description: The Paddling pre-session checklist: inspect every item, confirm fit, pack spares. PFDs are always worn; paddles are feathered. Five minutes of checking prevents the failures that ruin sessions — the forgotten mouthguard, the flat ball, the dead battery. Make the checklist a habit and the habit will save a season.
